question: A loss of 10(1)/(2)\% gets converted into a profit of 11(3)/(5)\% when the selling price is increased by Rs. 132.60. The cost price (in Rs.) the article is:
solution:
**Given:**

A loss of 10(1)/(2)\% gets converted into a profit of 11(3)/(5)\% when the selling price is increased by Rs. 132.60

**Concept used:**

SP = CP + CP × Profit%

SP = CP - CP × Loss%

**Calculation:**

Let CP of the article be 100a

Now,

SP for 1st case = 100a - 100a × 10(1)/(2)\%

⇒ 89.5a

SP for 2nd case = 100a + 100a × 11(3)/(5)\%

⇒ 111.6a

According to the question,

111.6a - 89.5a = 132.6

⇒ 22.1a = 132.6

⇒ a = 132.6/22.1

⇒ a = 6

So, cost price = 100 × 6

⇒ Rs. 600

**∴ The cost price (in Rs.) the article is 600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Loss = 10.5%, Profit = 11.6%

Overall profit increased = 11.6% - (- 10.5%) = 22.1%

22.1% = 132.6

1% = 6

100% = Rs. 600
